findings.problem: The trick links auf to English off, which teaches a false meaning: auf means up or on (ab is off), and aufgeben is literally up-give, give up.
findings.fix: trick: AUF means up and GEBEN means give, so aufgeben is literally to give up.

back.target: to give up (also to post a letter, to check luggage, to place an order)
back.example: Don't give up, you can do it!

note: The imperative example splits the separable verb correctly, and abandonar-abandon is close in meaning but not the same, so sameAs is right to be null.
